newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Quinn sees no abrupt end to EU aid for Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Quinn sees no abrupt end to EU aid for Ireland.

text.p: Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn said on Friday that European Union aid to the Irish economy would not be abruptly cut off because of its improving economic performance.

"There will be no abrupt change in EU funding," Quinn said at the end of a seminar on employment and structural funds. "The whole intention (of EU structural funding) was that there would be continuity and no abrupt change."
"Whatever the future may hold it will be a positive future," he said.
Monica Wulf-Mathies, EU Commissioner for regional policy, told a news conference that there would be no sudden change in EU support for the Irish economy
But she said: "Structural funding is not a permanent subvention and we do not want to create a dependency."
She lauded Ireland's economy, which has produced growth rates way above the EU average in recent years, and said she did not want to sever the aid lifeline
"It is important that we do not destroy with one hand what has been built up with the other," Wulf-Mathies said.
